correction.text: the Republic of Macedonia in the year of its independence (referendum of 8 September 1991): the same outline as Cliopatria's 1992 shape, only the years change

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria starts the state in 1992 although the page dates independence to 1991 ('declared independence and proclaimed as its official name the "Republic of Macedonia" in 1991').

1992-1999, 25,267 km2 against the infobox 25,436 km2 (ratio 0.99); the shape lies on Natural Earth's North Macedonia (bbox 20.5-22.9 E, 40.9-42.4 N). The UN admitted the state on 8 April 1993 as 'the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia'.

2000-2023, 25,125 km2: 142 km2 (0.6 percent) less than the 1992 shape, the same bbox. No page opened explains a change in 2000: the Kosovo page dates the Macedonia-Kosovo border dispute to the 2001 insurgency and a land exchange to October 2009, both later; I read the 2000 step as outline noise (Cliopatria's Kosovo row also begins in 2000) and keep the shape unverified at that precision.
2024, identical to the 2000 shape; the state is renamed Republic of North Macedonia in February 2019 without a change of border.

region.text: the republic within its federal borders; the page gives the referendum of 8 September 1991 and no boundary

ledger.note: 1991, 8 September: Macedonia votes for independence. Infobox 'Independence referendum: 8 September 1991'; the state 'officially celebrates 8 September 1991 as Independence day' and its federal entity 'declared independence and proclaimed as its official name the "Republic of Macedonia" in 1991'. The page gives no exact day for the declaration.

1993, 8 April: the state joins the UN as 'the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia'. 'North Macedonia became a member state of the UN on 8 April 1993'; 'in the period between 1991 and 2019, the country's name was an ongoing issue in bilateral and international relations'. Reviewer eu-22-f lowered confidence from 3 to 2: the page dates the UN admission under the provisional reference, but does not call it a change of the state's name; the constitutional name stayed 'Republic of Macedonia' until 2019 ('in the period between 1991 and 2019, the country's name was an ongoing issue'), so the 1993 label is a reading.

2019, February: the Republic of Macedonia becomes the Republic of North Macedonia. 'The Prespa agreement of June 2018 saw the country change its name to the "Republic of North Macedonia" eight months later'; 'on 12 February the Macedonian government announced the formal activation of the constitutional amendments' (the year of that sentence is inferred from the page's surrounding 2019 dates).

wars.name: 2001 insurgency in Macedonia
wars.outcome: A conflict 'between the government and ethnic Albanian insurgents' from February to August 2001; under the Ohrid Agreement 'the government agreed to devolve greater political power'. The page places the fighting 'mostly in the north and west of the country' but names no land the insurgents held, so zones are left empty pending the insurgency's own page (reviewer eu-22-f removed the draft's unsourced 'No territory changed hands').
wars.note: The Kosovo page adds that the insurgency started an eight-year border dispute with Kosovo that ended in October 2009 with an agreement to readjust the border 'by exchanging some land' (the page does not name the land); no ledger event can be placed for it.

certainty.note: The borders are the former republican borders of Yugoslavia. The Kosovo frontier is the exception: the Kosovo page calls the 2001-2009 dispute 'an eight-year-old border dispute', resolved in October 2009 by a land exchange that made 'the demarcation of the 150-kilometer border' possible.

notes: Two pages opened (budget 1-2). Cliopatria's two shapes both lie on the republic's border; the 2000 step (-142 km2) has no page behind it (see the keyframe). Not settled: the land exchanged with Kosovo in October 2009 (no page opened names it, so no ledger event; a gap-filler could open the Kosovo-Macedonia border agreement or the Cvetovo/Debelde sections), the date of the declaration of independence (the page gives the referendum, 8 September 1991, not the 17 or 25 September of other sources) and the date of the constitution. The 2001 insurgency is in wars with no zone because the page names no territory held by the insurgents. No ruler list opened. Slug note: the Cliopatria Name is 'Former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia', the display name is the current one.
